title: Interleaved batch steering - empirical notes
content:
Status: fresh experiment notes, lots of TODOs and open questions.

Summary:
This doc captures an ad-hoc investigation into how interleaved batching (multiple, small micro-batches scheduled across pipeline/tensor parallel stages) interacts with cross-GPU collectives and host<->device interconnects. Goal: find operational knobs that reduce p99 latency tail without sacrificing average throughput for medium sequence LLM inference (seq_len=512..2048).

Motivation & background:
- We keep seeing high p99s on dedicated pools when traffic is spiky. Median latency is fine but tails blow up.
- Hypothesis: when tensor-parallel (TP) + pipeline-parallel (PP) jobs interleave many small micro-batches, NCCL collectives and PCIe/NVLink contention cause microbursts and head-of-line blocking.
- This is different from the pure pipeline bubble problem; here the config interleaves micro-batches (to keep GPU utilization high under tight SLOs) but the interconnect/collectives scheduling is the choke.

Hardware / test rigs used:
- 2 nodes, each with 8x A100-40GB (PCIe + NVLink 3 links per GPU island), DGX-ish topology but not exact.
- Also a 4x A100 single-node config to validate intra-node NVLink behaviour.
- Network: 100GbE between nodes (routed), with RoCE disabled for these tests (we repeated with RoCE later).

Software stack:
- Serving runtime branch: feature/batch-steering-2024 (see linked PR).
- CUDA 12.2, cuDNN 9.x, NCCL 2.18.3 patched with our perf counters.
- Model: LLaMA-2 style 13B dense, 4-bit QAT variant used for throughput realism.
- Runner: local bench harness (serving/bench/bench_runner.py) that emits steady-state and spike workload patterns.

Experiment matrix (most important dimensions):
- TP degree: 1, 2, 4
- PP stages: 1, 2
- Micro-batch size: 1, 2, 4 tokens-per-microbatch (interpreted as micro request count; keep seq_len=1024 for all runs)
- Interleaving depth: none (strict per-stage flush), shallow (2 concurrent microbatches), deep (6 concurrent)
- NCCL algorithm hints: default, ALGO=ring, ALGO=tree-like (if available), and NCCL_P2P_LEVEL toggles
- Environment flags toggled: NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1, NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 vs ib0, NCCL_MAX_NRINGS=8, NCCL_MIN_NRINGS=2

Key commands and capture techniques:
- Bench run: python serving/bench/bench_runner.py --model llama-13b-q4 --tp 2 --pp 2 --micro 2 --interleave 6 --duration 600 --trace nsys
- nsys profile (short runs) to capture kernel timing + PCIe transfers. Also used nvlink-bandwidth-monitor in a loop to sample interconnect saturation.
- Custom NCCL logging built into our runtime (env NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and runtime logs to /tmp/nccl.log).

Representative results (abbrev, numbers are medians across three runs):
- Baseline (TP=2, PP=1, micro=2, interleave=2): p50=68ms, p95=210ms, p99=480ms, throughput=670 tps (tokens/sec).
- Deep interleave (TP=2, PP=2, micro=2, interleave=6): p50=73ms, p95=240ms, p99=900ms, throughput=880 tps. Note: higher throughput but p99 doubles.
- Increase micro-batch size to 4 while deep interleave: p50=95ms, p95=310ms, p99=520ms, throughput=980 tps. Observation: larger micro-batches reduce p99 even though median increases.
- Disable NVLink peer comms (force PCIe via NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1): p99 increases 30–50% for intra-node 4x config (expected).
- Ring algorithm vs default: little change for TP=1; for TP=4, ring reduced p95 by ~15% but p99 similar.

Interpretation / observations:
- Interleaving increases concurrency and throughput but creates more frequent small NCCL collectives (all-reduce/all-gather) with small message sizes. Small-message collectives are poorly amortized and sensitive to per-collective launch overhead and software scheduling jitter.
- Larger micro-batches turn several small collectives into fewer larger ones; increased median latency but much better tail behavior. For SLOs that care about p99, larger microbatch size may be preferable.
- We observed bursts of PCIe transmissions at the start of some microbatches (nsys traces) that coincided with 1–2x spike in CPU scheduling latency (sustained for ~3ms). Likely driver or NCCL thread scheduling on host is a contributor.
- For TP>2, algorithm choice and ring counts matter because we create many small inter-GPU exchanges that fragment into multiple rings; increasing NCCL_MAX_NRINGS improved throughput slightly but did not fix the tail.
- RoCE / RDMA enabled runs showed lower p50 and p95 but complicated failure modes under packet loss; we should only consider enabling with full network QoS.

Open questions / hypotheses to validate:
- Can we implement a microbatch coalescing layer in the runtime: buffer up to N microbatches (short timeout) and punch them through as a single collective (soft coalescing). Tradeoff: small added scheduling latency vs big tail wins.
- Is host-side NCCL thread scheduling the dominant source of jitter? Need a run with CPU affinity pinned for NCCL/UI threads and realtime priority.
- Do we see similar behaviour on H100 with NVLink-4 topologies? (we have queued tests)
- Can we leverage persistent kernels (pre-posted data) or GPUDirectRDMA to avoid PCIe bursts?

Short experiments to run next (actionable):
- (Connor) Pin NCCL threads + increase process niceness; repeat deep interleave runs and capture nsys. Target: 2024-11-05.
- (Miguel) Implement soft coalescing prototype in batch-steering branch (10ms max wait threshold), measure p99/throughput tradeoffs. Target: 2024-11-12 PR.
- (Rina) Validate RDMA/RoCE with QoS shaping on staging fabric (risk analysis). Target: 2024-11-07.

Notes to self / quick wins:
- In production, consider a dynamic policy: if p99 > target then enlarge micro-batch or reduce interleave depth for affected workers. This can be surfaced in Optimize recommendations.
- Instrument per-collective sizes in runtime traces (we currently log start/end but not message size). Add this.

Links / references within org:
- Bench harness: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tree/feature/batch-steering-2024/serving/bench
- Experiment ticket: RT-2143 (linked).

Unresolved: whether a kernel-level change (NCCL/persistent collectives) or runtime-level batching will be lower-risk to productize. My leaning: runtime soft-coalescing first for speed of iteration.

Last raw note: saw one run where p99 spiked to 2.3s and traced to one GPU running a long memcpy (host->device) while others were idle; need to capture host stack next time (strace, perf).

End of notes.

-- Aisha
